title: Intake contracts and compatibility matrix for variant-dependent open models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We currently lack a concise intake contract and automated checks for open-model variants whose compatibility with runtime optimizations (quantization, KV format, kernel constraints) is variant-dependent. This ambiguity leads to failed rollouts, last-minute pinning, and untracked regressions. Goal: Define a deterministic intake flow, metadata schema, and acceptance criteria so new open models and their variants can be onboarded with clear pin/fallback recommendations and automated compatibility gating. Deliverables: 1) Intake contract template (required fields, sample values) 2) Compatibility matrix for runtime features + clear pass/fail rules 3) Automated pre-onboarding checks (unit tests) integrated in model intake pipeline 4) Runtime fallback/pinning policy documented for catalog entries 5) Acceptance criteria and test harness for QA and SRE signoff.
scope: Author a one-page intake contract for community model submissions
Define canonical compatibility flags (e.g., kv_format, supports_kv_sharing, quantization_tolerance, attention_kernel_family, max_seq_len, dtype_profiles)
Specify deterministic pass/fail rules that map compatibility flags to recommended pinning/fallback policies
Ship a lightweight validation script used by model-onboarding that emits human-readable diagnostics and a catalog metadata artifact
Add acceptance tests to the onboarding CI that validate basic generation with pinned and fallback variants on a small sample prompt set
out_of_scope: Bulk model performance benchmarking (full perf harness) — only small smoke checks are required
Full automation of kernel selection in the serving runtime (handled by runtime team separately)
On-prem install packaging for private deployments — catalog metadata only
acceptance_criteria: Intake contract PDF + markdown template exists in Confluence and is linked from the intake UI
Compatibility schema v1 documented and added to the model catalog contract (fields and enums)
Validation script (python) runs in CI and returns non-zero on incompatible submissions; sample outputs added to repo
Three example community models (1 large decoder-only, 1 encoder-decoder, 1 alpaca-style fine-tune) have been processed end-to-end using the contract and pass smoke tests
Rollout guidance for each catalog entry produced: recommended pin, allowed fallbacks, and an explicit rollback trigger for quality regressions
SRE / Runtime review recorded in the ticket comments with signoff for schema and gating rules
risks: Overly strict pass rules may block high-value community models; need an exception path
Schema omissions could lead to silent incompatibilities at runtime (e.g., attention kernel mismatch)
Owners of downstream runtime features must commit to honoring compatibility flags; otherwise guidance will be ignored
